transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start: 09:17 PT
Duration: 47 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Marta Liu (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Sophie Grant (CSM), Ravi Patel (NetOps), Anika Shah (CTO), Marcus Lee (Security), Liam O'Connor (Platform), Jenna Morales (SRE)

Summary: quick sprint-5 checkin focused on connectivity regressions after kernel roll, telemetry gaps (missing egress tags), and fallback routing behavior. Agreed next steps on kernel patch, firewall CIDR list, and an end-to-end latency burn.

Topics: kernel compatibility, MTU and switching, VPC peering egress, fallback to hosted model, telemetry pipeline (trace IDs, tags), security audit log retention

Transcript:
[00:00] Marta (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanna run through sprint five items, connectivity, telemetry and the rollback options.
[00:28] Ravi (Arcadia NetOps): yep thanks, um quick note our morning run showed a few high tail latencies when the cluster hit 90% q depth, and a couple dropped requests -- could be MTU but maybe kernel.
[00:52] Devon (Redwood SE): got it. we saw similar in staging after the kernel upgrade, and there was an interaction with the continuous batching -- the K V cache indexing got a little, uh, misaligned.
[01:15] Anika (CTO): misaligned? can you say that again, i missed the detail, sorry.
[01:20] Devon (Redwood SE): sure so during the upgrade the kernel path changed the way NIC offloads behave, and that increased packet reassembly time on our qemu host which bumped p99 for some requests, so continuous batching would accumulate more in-flight tokens before flush. sounds like you're seeing that.
[01:43] Marcus (Security): i just wanna flag that any fallback to hosted must still satisfy our data retention and audit log controls, we've got a SOC2 window next quarter, so we need exact timelines.
[02:02] Marta (Redwood AE): yeah totally, that's why we proposed the Dedicated fallback only for non-sensitive routes or a filtered-copy path. we'll include audit log retention specifics in the followup security doc.
[02:20] Jenna (SRE): quick ops note, the switch team changed MTU from 9000 to 8972 for the last patch, so that might be the bit-rotten piece.
[02:36] Liam (Platform): 8972? that was an intermediate config for a vendor patch, we can revert but need to know if REDWOOD requires jumbo frames.
[02:47] Devon (Redwood SE): Redwood Private runtime prefers consistent MTU across the path for large KV cache transfers; jumbo frames help but are not strictly required. 1500 will work but you'll see a penalty in throughput for big tokens.
[03:10] Ravi (NetOps): okay, we'll reconfirm with switching and ping the exact MTU soon.
[03:18] Marta (Redwood AE): thanks. next, telemetry: Marcus pointed out we aren't seeing egress tags in traces, so when failover happened yesterday we couldn't tell which path served the request.
[03:33] Devon (Redwood SE): right, the tracer was emitting hostnames but not the routing tag because the agent sidecar didn't get the new env var after the ASG rolling update. small config miss.
[03:47] Anika (CTO): that sounds like a deploy-time problem, yeah. can you auto-inject that?
[03:53] Devon (Redwood SE): we can push a sidecar init that populates REDWOOD_ROUTE_TAG at pod start, yes. that'll retro-tag new spans; historical ones remain untagged.
[04:09] Ravi (NetOps): what about logs? our SIEM needs full audit for those fallback events.
[04:15] Sophie (CSM): we'll share the audit log retention SLA and the log forwarder config, and map fields to your SIEM schema.
[04:25] Marcus (Security): please include KMS key ids and whether logs contain PII by default.
[04:32] Marta (Redwood AE): noted, we'll add that to the security appendix.
[04:38] Liam (Platform): question on fallback: if Dedicated is unavailable do you route to Hosted by default, or do you do per-route policy?
[04:47] Devon (Redwood SE): it's policy driven. you can choose route-level fallback to Hosted, or canary to a quantized variant. for sensitive routes we recommend a filtered-copy to Hosted for telemetry only, not full payload.
[05:06] Anika (CTO): hmm filtered-copy for telemetry only sounds OK, but what's the latency hit? we need to keep 95th under 200ms for the product.
[05:16] Devon (Redwood SE): baseline is 120-140ms in-region with current quantization for most of your traces. the fallback to hosted adds roughly 30-50ms depending on egress path. if you account for our KV cache and prefix caching you'll see fewer full-model trips.
[05:36] Ravi (NetOps): we measured 210ms p95 during the incident window, that was with the older kernel setting.
[05:44] Devon (Redwood SE): okay so the kernel delta likely explains that. patching kernel should bring you back into the 140ms band.
[05:54] Marta (Redwood AE): let's talk schedule: we propose to deploy the kernel compatibility patch to the pilot cluster on Thursday (2026-12-02), run a staged burn on Friday, and then a full 50k token burn next Tuesday.
[06:08] Jenna (SRE): Thursday works but we'll need the exact patch binary and a rollback plan.
[06:15] Devon (Redwood SE): we'll provide the binary and a two-step rollback (revert kernel, revert agent). we'll also provide a procedure doc.
[06:25] Anika (CTO): good. on security: Marcus how much time do we need to validate log schema?
[06:32] Marcus (Security): a few days. if Redwood can supply sample logs and schema mapping by tomorrow we can run it through our audit tool.
[06:40] Sophie (CSM): i'll drop the schema mapping to the channel after the call.
[06:46] Marta (Redwood AE): perfect. now on the telemetry gap: Devon you mentioned retro-tagging won't catch the historical spans -- can we patch traces in our pipeline?
[06:57] Devon (Redwood SE): yes we can map trace IDs from request logs to reconstruct some spans if you forwarded request IDs. it's noisy but doable for the last 48 hours.
[07:10] Ravi (NetOps): we do forward request ids to the SIEM, i'll confirm retention window.
[07:15] Marcus (Security): also need to know encryption in transit for fallback copies. are they TLS 1.3 with mutual TLS?
[07:23] Devon (Redwood SE): yes mTLS for all cross-region fallback traffic; we can add your HSM KMS fingerprints to the keystore.
[07:33] Anika (CTO): thanks. turning to observability, we still see gaps in token-level cost instrumentation. we need per-route token breakdown to reconcile charges.
[07:45] Marta (Redwood AE): that's in Optimize; we can enable token-level tagging per route and share a sample billing breakdown.
[07:53] Liam (Platform): great, please include per-model and per-route columns, otherwise our finance team will ask questions.
[07:59] Sophie (CSM): yep will do.
[08:04] Ravi (NetOps): can we also get a gating rule so if p95 exceeds 250ms we automatically divert to fallback?
[08:12] Devon (Redwood SE): yes that's a circuit-breaker policy we can attach to the route in the console. we can tune hysteresis and cooldown to avoid flapping.
[08:24] Anika (CTO): and can that policy be scoped to only non-sensitive endpoints?
[08:30] Devon (Redwood SE): yep per-route scope. sensitive endpoints can have no-auto-fallback and instead alert only.
[08:38] Marta (Redwood AE): good. moving on, action items recap. Marta will send pricing for Dedicated fallback; Devon will run the 50k token benchmark; Liam will confirm MTU and switching notes; Sophie will share schema mapping.
[08:55] Marcus (Security): small point on retention windows - we need 13 months of audit logs, can Redwood support that on private?
[09:02] Devon (Redwood SE): yes we support customizable retention on Private; we'll list storage costs in the followup.
[09:10] Jenna (SRE): one more ops question, if we revert kernel do you expect any model incompatibilities?
[09:16] Devon (Redwood SE): no, the runtime is backward-compatible; the patch just adjusts NIC offload settings and kernel net stack behavior. we tested on a 2-node cluster.
[09:27] Ravi (NetOps): ok'll run the revert playbook if needed.
[09:30] Marta (Redwood AE): ok everyone, last thing - timeline and cadence. we keep weekly syncs but will add a short triage 15m next Friday if the burn test shows regressions.
[09:43] Anika (CTO): fine with me.
[09:46] Marta (Redwood AE): thanks all. we'll follow up in the channel with patch, docs, and schedule.
[09:52] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription errors: "K V cache" shows up as "K V cash" in some earlier logs; "Redwood Private" was transcribed once as "Redwood Privat". References to external artifacts: link to patch binary (s3://redwood-patches/arcadia/2026-12-02/kernel-compat-v1.tar.gz), telemetry schema doc (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/arcadia-telemetry-mapping), pricing spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/pricing/arcadia-dedicated-fallback.xlsx).

End of transcript.
